distractorExplanations.d: A clean-catch midstream specimen uses cleansing and a sterile cup but is a clean, not sterile, procedure.
distractorExplanations.a: The GI tract is not sterile, so NG tube insertion uses clean technique, unlike urinary catheter insertion.
distractorExplanations.c: A colostomy pouch change involves the GI tract and uses clean technique, not sterile technique.

options.d: Around age 65 for average-risk adults on Medicare

distractorExplanations.d: Age 65 is Medicare eligibility, not a screening start; USPSTF average-risk colorectal screening begins at 45.
distractorExplanations.a: Age 40 is the USPSTF start for biennial mammography, not colorectal screening.
distractorExplanations.c: Age 50 was the older USPSTF start; the 2021 update lowered it to 45 for average-risk adults.

options.a: Reposition the client by pulling on the weak arm, which has less pain sensation
options.b: Approach from the intact side and protect the weak side
options.c: Place food on the left side of the mouth and offer thin liquids
options.d: Hold the cane in the hand on the weak side and advance the strong leg first

distractorExplanations.a: Pulling on a weak arm can cause shoulder subluxation; reduced sensation increases injury risk.
distractorExplanations.c: Food goes on the unaffected (right) side, and thin liquids raise aspiration risk with dysphagia.
distractorExplanations.d: The cane is held on the strong side and advanced with the weak leg for support.
